verdict.rationale: Circle documents its own way to accept USDC payments: an x402 seller flow where your endpoint returns 402 Payment Required and serves the resource once a valid payment is attached. Generic webhooks also POST state changes to your endpoint. However, this flow is scoped to AI agents paying per request; nothing in the evidence shows a general customer checkout or payment-intent API that creates a payment, presents a deposit address, and confirms settlement. Missing for 10: a documented create-payment/checkout endpoint for human customers, a payment-address or hosted-flow presentation step, explicit payment-settlement confirmation events or status APIs, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can accept a stablecoin payment from a customer through a documented checkout or payment API — create the payment, present the address or flow, and confirm settlement programmatically

citations.quote: Make your API charge AI agents per request in USDC over x402: your endpoint returns 402 Payment Required when a request is unpaid, and serves the resource when a valid payment is attached.
When a resource changes state, Circle sends an HTTP POST to the endpoint you configure so your application can react.
